PROJECT 02 AUTOMATION

A world.
A bot. A plan.

A Minecraft bot that turns a goal into a sequence of actions: find resources, make tools, navigate terrain, and keep going when the world gets in the way. Built in Java, with its own pathfinding backend and an assisted TAS route.

The project botas · Minecraft 1.8 & 1.7.10

JavaPathfindingLegacy Fabric
Look under the hood ↗How I built it ↓
THE BUILD NOTESHow I built botas+

A GOAL IS ONLY THE BEGINNING

Teach it the steps.
Then teach it what goes wrong.

“Get an item” sounds simple until it needs ingredients, a tool, a furnace, and a way out of a hole. Botas connects those decisions to real player actions in Minecraft.

My work
Java automation & legacy integration
Foundation
Derived from AltoClef · MIT
Versions
1.8 main build · separate 1.7.10 port
01 / TURN GOALS INTO TASKS
Work backward from the item.

I use nested tasks to resolve recipe dependencies. The acquisition code checks inventory, finds ingredients, and delegates gathering, crafting, or smelting. It also guards against dependency loops and can abandon unnecessary work when the finished item is already available as a drop.

02 / FIND A WAY THROUGH
A navigation backend of its own.

Botas uses A* route planning with checks for the player’s body, floor support, and landing space. Movement follows waypoints, smooths clear stretches, and handles jumps and drops. When a walking route fails, it can look for an approach that safely clears blocks. It runs without a Baritone dependency.

03 / MAKE PROGRESS RELIABLE
The world gets a vote.

Getting stuck is part of the problem. The implementation tracks progress, rejects failed approaches, retries tasks, and waits for server state when needed. Inventory and pickup checks matter as much as the route: a plan can only continue once the required resources are actually there.

04 / CHAIN A LONGER ROUTE
From supplies to the End.

The 1.8 assisted TAS route connects natural chest loot, batched item-drop duplication, villager trading, tool crafting, a bed, stronghold travel, and End entry. Tick controls, player checkpoints, and planned pearl travel make individual stages easier to inspect and rehearse.

Read the goal→Resolve dependencies→Move & act→Verify progress
What this version does

The TAS route is assisted automation in a private world. Its default ending simulates the credits result after an in-game setup; @tasloot end stops at first End entry. The 1.7.10 port has a smaller feature set. These boundaries are documented alongside the commands.

PROJECT 04 GAME AI

The best move.
The worst intentions.

I built a pair of Python agents around opposite goals. Best Bot combines a complete first-player Connect 4 strategy with a fast search engine. Worst Bot looks ahead too — to give its opponent the win.

My work Strategy integration & search in Python

PythonGame theoryBitboards
Take on Best Bot ↗How I built it ↓
THE BUILD NOTESInside the minds of my Connect X bots+

THE AMBITION: BEST POSSIBLE PLAY

A solved strategy.
A very different kind of challenge.

Best Bot is built around a complete winning strategy for the first player in standard Connect 4. My Python agent combines that foundation with board validation, state recovery, and a search engine for positions outside the strategy.

Strategy foundation
Perfect first-player play · WeakC4
Standard setup
7 columns × 6 rows · connect 4 · bot first
Other modes
Timed search · connect 3, 4, or 5
01 / START WITH A SOLUTION
Know the winning continuation.

I embedded WeakC4’s first-player solution as compressed data inside a standalone Python file. The adapter reconstructs board positions from move histories, includes their mirror images, and follows compact rule diagrams when the game reaches them.

02 / KEEP THE STRATEGY HONEST
Match the actual game.

A remembered plan is only useful if it still fits the board. The agent validates the opponent’s move before reusing a diagram. If the Python module is reloaded between turns, it can reconstruct a compatible history by replaying the strategy and the opponent’s possible replies.

03 / SEARCH WHEN NEEDED
Look deeper without starting over.

For other positions, I use iterative-deepening negamax with alpha–beta pruning. Bitboards pack the position into integers for fast checks. A transposition table reuses previous results, while tactical pruning catches immediate wins, forced blocks, and moves that hand the opponent a winning threat.

04 / REVERSE THE OBJECTIVE
Make losing an engineering problem.

Worst Bot avoids taking its own immediate win whenever possible and looks for moves that give you a winning reply. Its bounded search rewards your threats and models a mix of strong and random replies. It can set up the opportunity; you still have to take it.

Read the board→Check tactics→Follow strategy / search→Return a legal column
Where “best possible” applies

WeakC4 supplies a complete winning strategy from the empty standard board as player one. That is the perfect-play foundation of this bot. Playing second, changing the target, or falling back after a strategy lookup timeout uses a time-limited search, which does not carry the same guarantee. Choose Connect 4 and Bot first to try the strategy-based challenge.

The actual Python. In your browser.

The game runs these original files through Pyodide in a background worker, so the interface stays responsive while an agent thinks. The strong agent searches for up to about 1.6 seconds per move with the current settings, keeping its best result from the last completed depth.

Challenge Best Bot ↗Best Bot source ↓Worst Bot source ↓

The solved strategy is by 2swap & the WeakC4 contributors, used under GPL-3.0. My work here is the Python adapter, state handling, search fallback, and the opponent-helping agent.
